Court No. - 69

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 29381 of 2023
Applicant :- Keshav

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Nitin Chandra Mishra,Manvendra Kumar Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Manvendra Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ajay Singh, learned
counsel for the State and perused the material on record.
2.

This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant-Keshav, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 195 of 2023, under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 4 D.P. Act, registered at P.S. Nebua Naurangia, District Kushinagar.

3. The first information report of the present matter was lodged on 16.05.2023 by the victim herself against the applicant and three others alleging therein that applicant is devar of her elder sister.
He used to visit her house.

In the month of June 2022, he came her house, while the victim was taking Keshav vs State Of U.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10697291/
1 bath, he clicked some photos and started threatening to viral the same and established physical relation with her forcibly.
He then stated of marrying her after which she stated to her parents and then proposal of marriage was discussed to his parents who refused it.
An application was given at the police station earlier on which parties had entered into compromise and were ready for marriage but subsequently they refused to marry and started talking for dowry.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the victim as per certificate of the Chief Medical Officer concerned has been opined to be above 18 as such she is major.

It is argued that in her statement 164 Cr.P.C.,
victim has stated that physical relationship between her and the applicant was established with consent but mother of the applicant had thrown her out of the house after which she came back to her house.
She stated that there was demand of dowry for getting married and the marriage could not materialize, hence, the present FIR has been lodged.
It is argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 12 of the affidavit and is in jail since 31.05.2023.
5. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument of the learned counsel for the applicant.

6. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that as per certificate of the Chief Medical Officer concerned victim is major; in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has stated of physical relationship with her consent; there was some discussion between the parties for marriage which could not materialize.

7. Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

8. Let the applicant Keshav, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.
In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his Keshav vs State Of U.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10697291/

2 presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(V) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A IPC.

(vi) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.
9.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
10. The bail application is allowed.

Order Date :- 20.7.2023 Mukesh Kr.
(Samit Gopal,J.)
